inputs.share_count_basis: 3,618,087,518 equity shares, basic = diluted (Q2 FY2027 interim statements, weighted average equals period-end; no employee stock plan). Held flat. The only potentially dilutive instrument is 1.26 crore Class B CCPS issued by the 85%-owned subsidiary HyperVault AI Data Center Ltd, which converts into subsidiary equity, not TCS shares; carried as debt at its INR 1,260m carrying value.
inputs.cash_composition_note: INR crore at 30-Sep-2026: cash and equivalents 5,106 + other bank balances 8,952 (less 607 earmarked/unclaimed-dividend balances, less 3,009 held by trusts and TCS Foundation) + current investments 40,582 (less 205 trust-held) + long-term bank deposits 512 (less 12 trust-held) + inter-corporate deposits 1,750 = 53,069 crore = INR 530,690m. Non-current investments (258, almost all trust-held) excluded. Borrowings are nil; total_debt is the Class B CCPS liability only. Lease liabilities (11,808 crore) are excluded because leases are charged in the flows.
inputs.fcf_bridge_note: FY2026: OCF 520,940 - capex 40,370 = reported FCF 480,570; less lease principal 18,610 and lease interest 7,780 (both in financing under Ind AS 116) = owner FCF 454,180. No SBC and no interest deduction: Ind AS OCF already excludes interest income (subtracted in the operating reconciliation, received in investing).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income was INR 38,540m but it is NOT inside reported OCF/FCF (classified in investing), and the forward build starts from EBITDA before other income, so there is nothing to strip. The matching asset (INR 530.7bn of liquid investments) is in the bridge exactly once.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in any cash flow statement FY2018-FY2027 H1; TCS has no employee stock plan. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: No buyback in FY2025, FY2026 or H1 FY2027 (last: INR 170,000m in FY2024, plus 39,590m buyback tax). Distribution is via dividends: INR 394,370m paid in FY2026.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z (15:28 IST, NSE regular session, last trade before the Friday close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows: India 10-year G-sec ~6.7% + equity risk premium ~6.0% (mature-market premium plus India country spread) x beta ~0.8 (debt-free, low-cyclicality large-cap IT services) = ~11.5% cost of equity; no borrowings so WACC = cost of equity. Same rate in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate. The ~2.5pp gap to a USD rate is the INR/USD inflation differential, which also appears in the revenue path as rupee depreciation on USD/EUR/GBP billings.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease principal + lease interest (FY2026: 18,610 + 7,780 = 26,390, 0.99% of revenue) deducted in the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2026 total D&A 55,600 less ROU depreciation ~18,640 = ~36,960, 1.38% of revenue; H1 FY2027 0.98%).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated. NCI (TCS Japan, C-Edge, HyperVault 15% etc.) earned INR 2,440m in FY2026 (0.5% of profit); deducted once in the equity bridge at 18x earnings rather than at INR 10,080m book.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US adaptations (INR-built WACC, single lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC-zero). Reason: TCS is a debt-free operating IT-services company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; none of the bank/REIT/LIC/holdco routes apply. First valuation of this ticker (fresh build). Currency: statements are INR (crore; stored as INR millions), NSE quote is INR, so currency == quote_currency and no FX bridge is needed; the economic exposure is ~95% non-INR billing, handled in the growth path. EBITDA in the CSV is before other income (FY2026: PBT pre-exceptional 700,130 + finance costs 12,270 + D&A 55,600 - other income 44,020 = 723,980), so investment income never enters the flows. FY2026 exceptional items (restructuring 11,350, Labour Code 21,280, legal-claim provision 10,100) and the H1 FY2027 legal settlement (6,680) are excluded from the margin base as non-recurring. Vintage mismatch, stated: year 1 is FY2027, half of which has elapsed; net cash is the 30-Sep-2026 balance, which already contains ~INR 71bn of retained H1 FY2027 cash flow, while year-1 FCF is discounted a full year although it completes in 4.5 months. The two roughly offset, with the net effect conservative. The price is a regular-session print, not after-hours. Working capital capture is negative (receivables + unbilled ~24% of revenue against payables and accruals; net operating working capital ~15% of revenue), so growth consumes cash. HyperVault AI Data Center (85% subsidiary, external preference capital) is the reason the capex path steps up above the 1.5% run-rate; H1 FY2027 capex was still ~1.5% of revenue.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at 18x FY2026 NCI profit (INR 2,440m)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 annual: profit attributable to NCI 244 crore; book NCI 1,008 crore at 30-Sep-2026. Charged once, here; flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: owner-FCF 3yr CAGR, cross-checked against revenue and EPS 3yr CAGRs (5.7-5.8%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (4.4%) diverges more than 30% from revenue (10.2%) and EPS (9.4%) 5yr CAGRs. Book value is not a usable growth anchor here: TCS distributes ~80-100% of profit through dividends and periodic buybacks, so equity barely compounds while the business does. Owner-FCF and revenue CAGRs used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less lease principal and lease interest; SBC nil; interest income already outside OCF): FY2021 ~339,400, FY2023 ~370,700, FY2026 454,180. FY2026 reported revenue growth of 4.6% was a 2.4% constant-currency DECLINE plus ~7pp of rupee depreciation; H1 FY2027 reported growth of 12.6% is likewise mostly currency (USD/INR ~94.5 against ~86.5 a year earlier) plus ~1pp from the ListEngage and Coastal Cloud acquisitions.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (FY2027): H1 actual revenue is INR 1,454,630m (+12.6%); H2 run-rate at ~INR 740-750bn a quarter against a second half of FY2026 that already carried part of the rupee move gives ~10%. Years 2-10: 3.5-5% constant-currency growth plus 2.5-3% a year of rupee depreciation (the INR/USD inflation differential embedded in the 11.5% rate), fading to 5%.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA before other income and before the lease charge: FY2022-FY2026 range 26.3-27.7%, FY2026 27.1%, H1 FY2027 25.7% as third-party and equipment costs rose with lower-margin revenue. Base settles at 26.5%, below the FY2026 peak, which was helped by a restructuring-led pyramid reset and currency.

scenario_narratives.base: Enterprise IT spending stays in cost-optimisation mode for another year or two, then normalises. Constant-currency growth recovers from FY2026's -2.4% to 3.5-5% as the US$40.7bn order book converts and AI-readiness work (cloud, data and mainframe modernisation) offsets productivity give-backs on run-the-business contracts; the rupee keeps depreciating at the inflation differential, adding 2.5-3 points to INR growth. Margins hold at 26.5% EBITDA (roughly a 24.5% EBIT margin, just under the FY2026 25.0% four-year high): AI-driven delivery productivity is shared with clients through pricing, and the employee pyramid reset done in FY2026 is not repeated. Capex rises from 1.5% to 2.5% of revenue for the HyperVault data-centre build, then settles at 2%.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI turns out to be a demand expander rather than a deflator for scaled integrators: enterprises need the data estate rebuilt, legacy cores modernised and agents run and governed, and TCS's annualised AI revenue (US$1.8bn at Q3 FY2026, above US$3.1bn and 10% of revenue by Q2 FY2027) compounds into a material share of the book. Vendor consolidation favours the largest incumbents, BFSI and the UK/Europe recover, and constant-currency growth runs 6-7% for five years on top of rupee depreciation. Fewer people per rupee of revenue lifts EBITDA to 27.5% and trims real-estate cost; HyperVault earns a return on a larger capex programme.
scenario_narratives.bear: Generative AI deflates the labour-arbitrage core faster than new work arrives: clients demand 20-30% productivity pass-through on renewals, application maintenance and BPO volumes shrink, the large deals that remain are won on price, and big clients take more work in-house through their own Global Capability Centres in India. Constant-currency revenue is flat to slightly negative for several years, so INR growth of 2.5-4% is entirely currency. Margins slide from 26% to 23.5% EBITDA as price cuts outrun headcount reduction and wage inflation continues, the US$100,000 H-1B application fee raises onsite delivery cost, and the data-centre capex earns a poor return. The exit multiple is capped at 16x because a no-growth-in-real-terms services firm does not earn a compounder's multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: there is no balance-sheet risk, but the bear case is not a cyclical dip, it is a structural one (AI deflating effort-based services) and the evidence so far points its way - FY2026 constant-currency revenue fell 2.4% and headcount was restructured. Base 50%: the order book, client stickiness and a decade of 26-28% EBITDA margins support continuity. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs AI demand to outrun AI deflation, a BFSI/Europe recovery and margin expansion simultaneously, and nothing in the last six quarters of constant-currency numbers shows it yet.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TCS is valued as a debt-free cash machine: nearly all profit converts to free cash and is paid out, so the value is the INR owner-FCF stream plus ~INR 146 a share of net liquid assets. The reported INR growth rate flatters the business because most of it is rupee depreciation on foreign-currency billings; the model keeps that in the growth path only because the discount rate is an INR rate that already charges for it. The live question is whether AI expands or deflates the services pool, which is what separates the three scenarios.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI-driven price deflation in application maintenance, testing and BPO work outrunning new AI-services demand (the bear axis)
Reported growth is currency: a stable or appreciating rupee would cut INR growth to the constant-currency rate, which was negative in FY2026
Terminal value is the majority of enterprise value and is sensitive to the 5% INR terminal growth and the 11.5% rate
HyperVault AI data-centre programme changes the capital intensity of an asset-light business; returns are unproven and the subsidiary carries external convertible preference capital
Client concentration in North American and UK/European BFSI; US immigration and outsourcing-tax policy raising onsite delivery cost
H1 FY2027 EBITDA margin (25.7%) is already below the 26.5% base steady state; the base case assumes partial recovery
